subject: Testing the Statistical Significance of an Added Factor

messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Testing the Statistical Significance of an Added Factor
parts:
Hi Phil,

When comparing models with different number of factors in exploratory IRT, is mirt's anova() is equivalent to the formula (28) in the paper High-dimensional maximum marginal likelihood item factor analysis by adaptive quadrature? This method is used to choose number of factors, as mentioned in Reckase's book Multidimensional item response theory (p. 218). Thanks.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Testing the Statistical Significance of an Added Factor
parts:
Yes it is the same, but I wouldn't recommend using it for testing for more dimensions. Increases in dimensions are not nested, so you would be better to check information criteria instead (BIC is generally what I prefer, to keep the model complexity as simple as possible in exploratory settings). That formula is really only useful when testing nested parameter constraints, where large sample likelihood theory applies. Cheers.

Phil
